name: Hawke's Bay Nature Fund
summary: Annual NZ fund for predator control and revegetation projects that create habitat in Hawke's Bay, with a rotating priority area. Projects start at NZD 25,000 and run up to three years.
reporting: Quarterly progress reports and a final report on completion

eligibility.rule: Project focuses on pest control and/or revegetation
Project is within the priority area specified for this financial year
Project supports DOC's regional strategy and Hawke's Bay plan outcomes
Project will be sustained by the applicant after funding ends
Project runs for one, two or three years
Applicant has the required project Health and Safety plan and land permissions
Applicant and project operator are the same individual or group
Excludes retrospective costs, paid landowner or volunteer time, and work required by law

documents: Evidence of project support by the land manager, for another agency's land
Written land manager confirmation of Health and Safety duties, for private or public land
DOC Hawke's Bay Community Agreement, for public conservation land
Evidence of DOC Hawke's Bay Operations Manager support, for public conservation land

opens.quote: The Hawke's Bay Nature fund 2026 key dates 8th June - Application portal opens 20th July - Application portal closes at 5pm

deadline.quote: The Hawke's Bay Nature fund 2026 key dates 8th June - Application portal opens 20th July - Application portal closes at 5pm

administered_by.quote: The fund is managed by the Eastern and Central Community Trust.

applicant_types.quote: Community groups, private landowners, iwi, and agencies throughout Hawke's Bay can apply for the funding.

geography.quote: The Hawke's Bay Nature fund is confined to conservation efforts within the DOC Hawke's Bay District boundary.

access.quote: All applications must be made via the Fluxx grants portal.

amount.quote: The Hawke's Bay Nature Fund will fund projects of $25,000 and over.

pool.quote: Approximately $500,000 will be allocated annually to projects of $25,000 and over.

window.quote: The Hawke's Bay Nature fund 2026 key dates 8th June - Application portal opens 20th July - Application portal closes at 5pm

reporting.quote: Grantees will be required to report quarterly on the progress of their project and provide a final report on completion of the project.

effort.quote: Applications must be submitted no later than 5pm 20th July 2026.
All eligible applications are assessed by a Grant Committee against the fund's assessment criteria and based on their merit compared with other applications.

eligibility.quote: Your project focusses on pest control and/or revegetation
Your project is within the priority area specified for this financial year
Your project supports the achievement of the outcomes for Hawke's Bay as defined in the Department of Conservation's Lower North Island Regional Strategy and Plan and the Hawke's Bay Multi-Year Plan
You are seeking funding to boost a project that will be sustained by you / your group once funding has concluded
You are seeking funding for one, two or three years.
You have a Health & Safety plan for your project (and owner consent if on the land of another agency, or approval in principle to develop a Community Agreement if on Public Conservation Land)
The individual or group applying to the Fund must be the same individual or group who will run the project.

retrospective costs (i.e. costs incurred prior to a Deed of Grant being signed) • reimbursement of landowner time or voluntary labour • activities that individuals, organisations or councils are required to do by law

after_award.quote: Grantees will be required to report quarterly on the progress of their project and provide a final report on completion of the project.
They will also conduct quarterly visits to your site so they can report on your project to ECCT.

documents.quote: All applicants will be required to submit a project-specific Health and Safety Plan as part of the application.
Project Budget & quotes Project Sustainability Plan Proof of bank account The documents I must attach to my application are: Evidence that the project is supported by the land manager

You will need to provide written confirmation from the land manager / authorised representative that they are complying with their duties and obligations under the Health and Safety Work Act 2015 in respect of you working on the land they administer/manage.

You must already have permission before applying to the Fund and must attach your Community Agreement to your application. You must also supply evidence that the DOC Hawke's Bay Operations Manager supports your application.
